title: 3. Test insertion specificity with an expert-calibrated hard-task scan
hypothesis: Assembly exposes a precision-insertion limitation rather than generic manipulation difficulty, so searched structures will solve impact tasks more often than side insertion.

prediction.rationale: The prespecified contrast is mean hammer-and-soccer success minus peg-insert-side success; a +0.50 gap would distinguish contact regimes rather than merely discover another isolated failure.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (--research-mode contact-regime-scan: expert calibration first, one structure per task, 24-candidate search, Welch impact-minus-insertion contrast)

falsified_by: With expert success at least 0.90 on the three contrast tasks, a contrast interval upper bound below +0.50 refutes the predicted separation. An interval including zero is inconclusive about a regime difference. Failed expert calibration makes the mechanism inconclusive pending a source-verified expert success measurement on the affected task.

result.notes: Expert calibration on each task's 30 frozen screen cases (pools 3540, 3541, 3544): hammer-v2 1.00, soccer-v2 0.90, peg-insert-side-v2 0.63. The gate requires >= 0.90 on all three, so per the protocol no structure was generated and the contact-regime contrast is inconclusive. The first launch stopped before any rollout because EXPERT_POLICY_MAP lacked peg-insert-side-v2 (added: SawyerPegInsertionSideV3Policy); the relaunch reused the frozen manifests. Missing measurement: a source-verified expert success measurement for peg-insert-side-v2 (MetaWorld's scripted expert reaches only 0.63 on these placements). 90 episodes, 0 LLM calls.

verdicts.reasoning: The predeclared calibration gate failed: MetaWorld's scripted expert solved only 0.63 of peg-insert-side-v2's 30 screen cases (hammer 1.00, soccer 0.90), so the protocol stopped before generation. No learner data exist; the contact-regime contrast is untested.
verdicts.next_experiment: Either drop peg-insert-side as the insertion control (use a task whose expert is reliable) or accept a lower calibration bar; hammer (1.00) and soccer (0.90) are calibrated and could be scanned as further testbeds.

verdicts.reasoning: Peg-insert-side expert success was 0.6333, below the required 0.90 calibration gate [logs/next_contact_regimes_s3540/summary.json]. Hammer and soccer passed at 1.00 and 0.90, respectively, but calibration required every contrast task to pass [logs/next_contact_regimes_s3540/summary.json]. No learner arm ran, so the prediction's peg-insert-side control and impact-minus-insertion screen_success_rate contrast were not measured [logs/next_contact_regimes_s3540/summary.json]. The prediction is therefore neither supported nor refuted; these expert measurements do not establish a learner contact-regime difference [logs/next_contact_regimes_s3540/summary.json].
